citations.quote: In order to reduce ambiguity and alleviate functional couplings, this paper integrates AD with the MBSD and proposes a unified systems design approach, called Axiomatic Model-Based Systems Design (A-MBSD).

The development of a large-scale product such as an automobile, a satellite, or an airplane has evolved to employ a systems engineering methodology, in which systems design (SD) performs a crucial role through the explicit representations of system requirements and overall solutions that have a profound influence on subsequent integration, verification, validation, and operation.
Ambiguity tends to arise when information is scattered throughout a disjointed set of text documents, spreadsheets, and diagrams.

Finally, the proposed method is demonstrated by the design of a Forest Fire Satellite Monitoring and Control System (FFSMCS), which shows that the method can improve design unity and alleviate unnecessary, nonintrinsic couplings during SD.
A-MBSD is a top-down, iterative process as shown in Figure 3, and it consists of a SD process and a domain-specific design process.

SD starts by analyzing requirements, which analyzes the provided mission and creates a customer domain (CD). Designers then translate CNs into a set of functional, performance requirements, and constraints.

In system function analysis and allocation, first, a designer defines use cases (UCs) according to FRs. Then, the designer analyzes these UCs through an action response, message transfer, and state change to create a BD shown by the dashed ellipse in Figure 3.

Before defining alternative solutions, a designer can identify functional couplings by the design matrix that represents the realizing relationships between FRs and DPs. Only designs conforming to the Independence Axiom can be considered as alternatives.
When [A] is diagonal, the design is said to be ideal; thus, designers further decompose DPs and FRs, and initiate the next iteration.
When [A] is triangular, the design is said to be decoupled. Designers should realign DPs to obtain independent FRs.
The design is coupled in other situations. Designers have to reselect DPs in order to remove the impacts that DPs have on different FRs until FRs stay independent from each other.

SysML is selected for modeling the system model of A-MBSD to keep it unified, because it has been designed to enable extensions that support specialized concepts such as design domains and axioms of AD by its own extension mechanism, called stereotyping.

The definition of a mapping profile is described in Figure 9. According to the AD zigzag process, two kinds of mapping relationships: (a) mapping at the same level and (b) mapping between two different levels, are named as H mapping and V mapping, respectively, by extending the «dependency» relationship.
Accordingly, in the following sections, the A-MBSD is applied to the SD of a virtual FireSAT mission.
An assumed FireSAT project, called FFSMCS, is aimed at monitoring daily forest fires and informing local forestry departments of these fires to be able to control them in time.

The proposed A-MBSD is thus applied to the FFSMCS to illustrate how the RFBS documents SD information explicitly helping designers to make decisions through building design matrixes and using the Independence Axiom.
